title: Refining the booking search
idea: Refinement is changing a working design to be clearer or faster without changing its behaviour; optimization is the part driven by a measured bottleneck.
points: Measure first: count work done, such as bookings read, before guessing at slowness.
`searchFree` scanned every booking for every room; an index per room removes that.
The change stays inside `BookingRepository`, so callers and tests stay as they are.
State the trade-off aloud: more memory and an invariant for fewer reads.

steps.caption: Start only from passing tests. They define the behaviour the refactor must keep.
Count the work one `searchFree` call does. A count is repeatable; a stopwatch is not.
The count points at `forRoom`: it walks every booking of every room, once per room.
Change one thing: index bookings by room, sorted by start time, inside the repository.
Re-run the tests and compare the free-room list. Same answer means same behaviour.
Measure again. Keep the change only if the count dropped and the code is still clear.
Then look for the next hotspot, or stop when the count is good enough.

code.title: Before: one flat list
code.caption: Forty rooms, seven bookings each. Correct results, but every `forRoom` call walks the whole list.

walk.text: Fixed test data: each room has one free hour, so the output is the same on every run.
The same `ConflictPolicy` that `book` uses. Search must never invent its own overlap rule.
Every booking of every room sits in one list. `reads` counts the work instead of timing it.
`forRoom` reads other rooms' bookings only to skip them. That is the hotspot.
Note the free list and the read count. The refactor must match the first and shrink the second.

code.title: After: a sorted index per room
code.caption: Same data, same `SearchService` and policy, a different repository inside. Each call reads one room only.

walk.text: A map from room to a `TreeMap` keyed by start time. Finding a room's bookings needs no scan.
`computeIfAbsent` creates a room's map on its first booking, so no room needs pre-registering.
`forRoom` keeps its contract: that room's bookings, now sorted by start. Only they are counted.
Keying by start is safe only because `book` rejects clashes before `save`. Write the invariant down.
Search still asks `policy.conflicts`, exactly as in c11-t04, so search and `book` cannot disagree.
The policy is untouched. Swap in another one and both search and booking follow it.

pitfalls: Keying by start silently replaces a same-start booking; reject clashes before every save.
Adding a faster overlap check inside the repository makes search list rooms `book` rejects.
Optimizing before measuring adds complexity to code that was never slow; show the count first.

quiz.q: Room R1's index gets three saves. What does this print?
quiz.why: A `TreeMap` orders by key, and `put` on an existing key replaces its value. B3 silently overwrote B1, which is why clashes must be rejected first.

takeaway: Measure, change one thing behind the interface, prove behaviour is unchanged.

starters: How do I explain time complexity of searchFree in an interview?
Would an interval tree be better than a TreeMap here?
How do I make the indexed repository safe for concurrent bookings?
